senses.definition: An amount of money paid to a worker for a specified quantity of work, usually calculated on an hourly basis and expressed in an amount of money per hour.
senses.example: Before her promotion, her wages were 20% less.
My life I never held but as a pawn / To wage against thine enemies

senses.definition: To expose oneself to, as a risk; to incur, as a danger; to venture; to hazard.
senses.example: I fear the power of Percy is too weak / To wage an instant trial with the King.

senses.definition: To employ for wages; to hire.
senses.example: Thenne said Arthur I wille goo with yow / Nay said the kynges ye shalle not at this tyme / for ye haue moche to doo yet in these landes / therfore we wille departe / and with the grete goodes that we haue goten in these landes by youre yeftes we shalle wage good knyghtes & withstande the kynge Claudas malyce

senses.definition: To conduct or carry out (a war or other contest).
senses.example: pond'ring which of all his Sons was fit / To Reign, and wage immortal War with Wit

senses.definition: To adventure, or lay out, for hire or reward; to hire out.
senses.example: Thou that doest liue in later times, must wage / Thy workes for wealth, and life for gold engage.

senses.definition: To give security for the performance of.
